verses.zh: 耶和华的灵（原文是手）降在我身上。耶和华藉他的灵带我出去，将我放在平原中；这平原遍满骸骨。
verses.en: The hand[NOTE:1] of the Lord was on me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of the Lord and placed[NOTE:2] me in the midst of the valley, and it was full of bones.
notes: Or “power.” sn Hand in the OT can refer metaphorically to power, authority, or influence. In Ezekiel God’s hand being on the prophet is regularly associated with communication or a vision from God (3:14, 22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1).
Heb “caused me to rest.”
verses.commentary:
37:1 "The hand of the Lord was upon me" This has been a recurrent literary marker
of a new revelation (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 3:14,22; 8:1; 33:22; 37:1; 40:1).

Special Topic: Hand

Special Topic: Ways of Revelation

▣ "by the Spirit of the Lord" The word "Spirit" in Ezek. 37:1, 14 and
the word "breath" in Ezek. 37:5, 6, 8, 9 (twice), and 10 and the word "wind" in Ezek. 37:9 all relate to one Hebrew term,
ruah (BDB 924), which can mean "wind, breath, or spirit." There is a play on this root throughout this chapter.

Special Topic: Spirit (pneuma) in the Bible

Special Topic: Breath, Wind, Spirit

▣ "the valley" This seems to refer to the place of slaughter (cf. Jer. 7:32-8:2). The place of
idolatry and judgment (i.e. Jerusalem, the Valley of Topheth, Valley of the Sons of Hinnom, Gehenna) will become
the very place of resurrection and restoration.

The real question is to whom does this refer?

- past idolatrous leaders and Israelites (cf. Jer. 7:37-8:2)

- current Judeans

- the righteous remnant (see
Special Topic: The Remnant,
Three Senses)

- future Jews

- symbol of God's people (cf. Ezek. 37:11)

but not previous idolaters. It seems to me in context that #3 fits best. It is texts like this
that cause some to say all Jews will be saved, but this violates too many NT texts, even the Jews of Romans 9-11
(as well as those of Zech. 12:10) must be repentant believers (cf. Jer. 3:22-4:2). There is no biblical support
for the restoration of unbelieving, unrepenting descendants of Abraham. Only the people of faith are his
true seed (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; Gal. 6:16). Remember that chapter 36 (i.e. new heart, new spirit) sets the
contextual stage for chapter 37.

The term "valley" in Ezek. 37:1 is BDB 132 (which can refer to a broad plain, LXX), while Jer. 7:32 is
BDB 161. However, they may still relate to one another.

verses.zh: 他使我从骸骨的四围经过，谁知在平原的骸骨甚多，而且极其枯干。
verses.en: He made me walk all around among them.[NOTE:1] I realized[NOTE:2] there were a great many bones in the valley, and they were very dry.
notes: Heb “and he made me pass over them, around, around.”

The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and is here translated as “I realized” because it results from Ezekiel’s recognition of the situation around him. In Hebrew, the exclamation is repeated in the following sentence.

verses.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，这些骸骨能复活吗？」我说：「主耶和华啊，你是知道的。」
verses.en: He said to me, “Son of man, can these bones live?” I said to him, “Sovereign Lord, you know.”

verses.zh: 他又对我说：「你向这些骸骨发预言说：枯干的骸骨啊，要听耶和华的话。
verses.en: Then he said to me, “Prophesy over these bones, and tell them: ‘Dry bones, listen to the Lord’s message.
verses.commentary:
37:4 Notice that the Spirit (wind, breath) and the Word (note Ezek. 37:14) of the Lord
are parallel (cf. Isa. 59:21). As God (i.e. Jesus, cf. John 1:3,10; Rom. 11:36; 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16; Heb. 1:2; 2:10)
breathed into the newly formed human body (cf. Gen. 2:7) to create persons for fellowship, so He does again!

This emphasizes the power of the Word of God (cf. Ezek. 6:3; 13:2,6; 16:35; 20:47; 25:3; 34:7,9;
36:1; Isa. 45:23; 55:11; Matt. 24:35). This is a re-creation event!

verses.zh: 主耶和华对这些骸骨如此说：『我必使气息进入你们里面，你们就要活了。
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says to these bones: Look, I am about to infuse breath[NOTE:1] into you and you will live.
notes: Heb “I am about to bring a spirit.”
verses.commentary:
37:5 This is parallel to Gen. 2:7 (notice Ezek. 37:8); there by God (i.e. Jesus) and here by His
Spirit (cf. Ezek. 37:14). Only God can give and sustain life! Only He has life! Here the "life" is national
restoration to the Promised Land. The reversal of exile (national death) by the renewal of the covenant
promises (conditional on covenant obedience, cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28).

Special Topic: Covenant

Special Topic: Keep

verses.zh: 我必给你们加上筋，使你们长肉，又将皮遮蔽你们，使气息进入你们里面，你们就要活了；你们便知道我是耶和华。』」
verses.en: I will put tendons[NOTE:1] on you and muscles over you and will cover you with skin; I will put breath[NOTE:2] in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the Lord.’”
notes: The exact anatomical referent of the term is uncertain. In addition to v. 8, the term occurs only in Gen 32:32 (32:33 Heb); Job 10:11; 40:17; Is 48:4.
Or “a spirit.”
verses.commentary:
37:6 This is a recurrent theme, usually connected to judgment (i.e. Ezek. 35:9; 38:23; 39:6),
but here to symbolic resurrection of a whole people (i.e. Joel 2:27; 3:17). In Isaiah 49 this phrase is
linked to the inclusion of the Gentiles (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13). This has always been God's plan!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan.

verses.zh: 于是，我遵命说预言。正说预言的时候，不料，有响声，有地震；骨与骨互相联络。
verses.en: So I prophesied as I was commanded. There was a sound when I prophesied— I heard[NOTE:1] a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
verses.commentary:
37:7 "a noise" The term (BDB 876) can refer to

- a human voice (Ezek. 27:30; 33:32)

- a sound (cf. Gen. 3:8,9)

- the Lord's voice (Isa. 6:8)

- Cherubim wings (Ezek. 1:24; 3:13; 10:5)

- Seraphim's voice (Isa. 6:4)

- angel (Dan. 8:16)

- animals/chariots (Ezek. 3:13)

- musical instrument

- thunder

- lament (Ezek. 26:15; 31:16)

BDB (#2g) calls it an earthquake. However, the context implies it was the sound (i.e. rattling)
of bones coming together. That these unburied bones could live again is amazing symbolism of restoration and
forgiveness of the covenant people (both corporate and individual).

▣ "a rattling" In Ezek. 12:18 this same word (BDB 950) is used of fear and trembling. It can
also refer to an earthquake (cf. 1 Kgs. 19:11,12; Isa. 29:6; Ezek. 38:19; Amos 1:11; Zech. 14:5). These
bones made a lot of noise as they assembled themselves.

verses.zh: 我观看，见骸骨上有筋，也长了肉，又有皮遮蔽其上，只是还没有气息。
verses.en: As I watched, I saw[NOTE:1] tendons on them, then muscles appeared,[NOTE:2] and skin covered over them from above, but there was no breath[NOTE:3] in them.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Heb “came up.”
Or “spirit.”
verses.commentary:
37:8 Apparently the bones were scattered on the ground. At Ezekiel's prophesying they came together
as a complete skeleton, but still lying on the ground (cf. Ezek. 37:10b). This cannot be used as a proof-text that Israel
will return to the Promised Land unconverted (i.e. The Prophecy of Ezekiel by Charles Lee Feinberg, p. 213. See
YouTube video by Steve Gregg, "The Modern State of Israel."

verses.zh: 主对我说：「人子啊，你要发预言，向风发预言，说主耶和华如此说：气息啊，要从四方（原文是风）而来，吹在这些被杀的人身上，使他们活了。」
verses.en: He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath[NOTE:1]—prophesy, son of man—and say to the breath: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these corpses so that they may live.’”
notes: Or “spirit,” and several times in this verse.
verses.commentary:
37:9 "say to the breath" This verse has five commands.

- "prophesy," BDB 612, KB 659, Niphal IMPERATIVES directed
to Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 37:12)

- "come," BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "breathe," BDB 655, KB 708, Qal IMPERATIVE directed to the
breath/wind/spirit (see Special Topic: Breath, Wind, Spirit)

- "come to life," BDB 310, KB 309, Qal IMPERFECT used
in a JUSSIVE sense to the newly formed bodies

This word "breath" can also be translated "wind," "spirit." Notice this breath is personified (see Special Topic: Breath, Wind, Spirit).

- It comes from the four corners of the earth (cf. Isa. 43:5).

- It breathes breath on the inanimate human bodies.

- It comes into the human bodies (Ezek. 37:10) and brings life.

This is all parallel to Genesis 2 (esp. Ezek. 37:7). This is new life before the Fall, a new
chance at obedience with a new heart and a new spirit (i.e. Ezek. 36:22-36)!

▣ "from the four winds" This is imagery for all directions. The exiles will return from all
directions; the Spirit is with them and will bring them home.

Note the enemies of chapters 38-39 are also from all directions. Evil is also pervasive!

Special Topic: Symbolic Numbers in Scripture, #2

verses.zh: 于是我遵命说预言，气息就进入骸骨，骸骨便活了，并且站起来，成为极大的军队。
verses.en: So I prophesied as I was commanded, and the breath came into them; they lived and stood on their feet, an extremely great army.
verses.commentary:
37:10 "an exceedingly great army" Although this Hebrew term (BDB 298) can mean "army" (i.e.
Ezek. 17:17; 27:10), it can be understood as a multitude (cf. NRSV, note Ezek. 37:11). The new Israel
does not need a great army, they have a great God (this is why chapters 38-39 are so surprising)!

verses.zh: 主对我说：「人子啊，这些骸骨就是以色列全家。他们说：『我们的骨头枯干了，我们的指望失去了，我们灭绝净尽了。』
verses.en: Then he said to me, “Son of man, these bones are all the house of Israel. Look, they are saying, ‘Our bones are dry, our hope has perished; we are cut off.’
verses.commentary:
37:11 "these bones are the whole house of Israel" This is YHWH's promise that the northern and southern tribes,
split since 922 B.C., will be reunited (cf. vv. 15-23; Jer. 3:18; 23:5-6; 50:4-5; Hosea 1:11) under a Davidic king.

▣ "we are completely cut off" There is a possible manuscript issue in this phrase.

NASB "we are completely cut off"

NKJV "we ourselves are completely cut off"

NRSV "we are cut off completely"

LXX "we are quite spent" or "we are lost"

Peshitta "we are completely gone"

JPSOA "we are doomed"

The Tyndale OT Commentary Series, Ezekiel, by John Taylor mentions that
F. Perles redivides the phrase to "our thread-of-life has been cut off" (238), which fits the context better
than "we have been cut off for us" (Niphal PERFECT).

This refers to the Judean's view of themselves in light of the destruction of Jerusalem and the
temple and the exile of the Davidic King. There was no hope humanly speaking (cf. Ezek. 19:5)!

verses.zh: 所以你要发预言对他们说，主耶和华如此说：『我的民哪，我必开你们的坟墓，使你们从坟墓中出来，领你们进入以色列地。
verses.en: Therefore prophesy, and tell them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look, I am about to open your graves and will raise you from your graves, my people. I will bring you to the land of Israel.
verses.commentary:
37:12-14 These are covenant promises (i.e. the land, cf. Ezek. 37:12,14) and covenant title
(i.e. "My people," Ezek. 37:12,13). The covenant is renewed! Destruction and exile have ceased.

Again one asks the question, when did or will this occur?

- post-exilic return under Zerubbabal (seed of David) and Joshua (seed of High Priest)

- some future time (see my new verse-by-verse commentary on the book of Revelation online at www.freebiblecommentary.org)

Because Israel was attacked again by Rome and the temple destroyed again (A.D. 70,
cf. Dan. 9:24-27), many modern interpreters assert a future orientation. There are certainly eschatological elements in chapters
36-48! My focus is on the conditional nature of prophecy. This reflects what God wanted His people to be and do, as well as what
He wanted to do for them, but Genesis 3 (the Fall; see Special Topic: The Fall of Mankind)
got in the way. Mankind's fallen propensities can be dealt with only by the Messiah's work and the new age (new covenant). Chapter 36
surely reflects this, but what of chapters 38-39? Israel is attacked again by surrounding enemies. Security is challenged!

The question is, "Was the opposition caused by

- Israel's continuing sin

- evil's attack on God?"

Number 1 fits the post-exilic period (cf. Malachi).

The hard question is, "Must all prophecy be literally fulfilled to Israel?" I think not (i.e. Jonah, see
Special Topic: Prophecy [OT])! The NT focuses on Jesus, not Israel. The
NT widens the OT promises to all humans. The national and/or geographic promises to Israel are not repeated or mentioned by Jesus nor
any of the Apostles or NT authors! This is very surprising, but true.

Special Topic: Why Do OT Covenant Promises Seem So Different from NT Covenant Promises?

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

37:12 "Thus says the Lord God" This recurrent literary phrase introduces
(list from NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 445)

- judgment against the surrounding nations (cf. Ezek. 25:3; 30:2)

- judgment against individuals (cf. Ezek. 28:2; 39:1)

- judgment against Judah (cf. Ezek. 5:8; 12:19)

- her mountains, Ezek. 6:3

- her false religious leaders, Ezek. 13:3,18

- her faithlessness, Ezek. 20:30

- her injustices, Ezek. 45:9

- call for Judah to repent (cf. Ezek. 14:6)

- message of restoration and forgiveness (cf. Ezek. 36:33; 37:12,21; 39:25)

- message of hope to Ezekiel himself (cf. Ezek. 2:4; 3:11)

▣ "I will open your graves and cause you to come up out of your graves" This refers to an image of
Abraham's seed being restored to Canaan. This is not an OT reference to individual resurrection, though later rabbis
tried to use it in this sense (i.e. Sanh. 10:1 and b.Sanh. 90b).

Special Topic: Ressurection, II.

Special Topic: Pharisees

▣ "the land of Israel" both Hebrew words for "land" are used in chapter 37.

- Adamah (BDB 9, KB 15), which is used for Canaan, vv. 12,14,21

- erets (BDB 75, KB 90) used in v. 25 where it is also used of Canaan

Special Topic: World (several terms)

Special Topic: Covenant Promises to the Patriarchs

verses.zh: 我的民哪，我开你们的坟墓，使你们从坟墓中出来，你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: Then you will know that I am the Lord, when I open your graves and raise you from your graves, my people.

verses.zh: 我必将我的灵放在你们里面，你们就要活了。我将你们安置在本地，你们就知道我―耶和华如此说，也如此成就了。这是耶和华说的。』」
verses.en: I will place my breath[NOTE:1] in you and you will live; I will give you rest in your own land. Then you will know that I am the Lord—I have spoken and I will act, declares the Lord.’”
notes: Or “spirit.” This is likely an allusion to Gen 2 and God’s breath that creates life.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要取一根木杖，在其上写『为犹大和他的同伴以色列人』；又取一根木杖，在其上写『为约瑟，就是为以法莲，又为他的同伴以色列全家』。
verses.en: “As for you, son of man, take one branch and write on it, ‘For Judah and for the Israelites associated with him.’ Then take another branch and write on it, ‘For Joseph, the branch of Ephraim, and all the house of Israel associated with him.’
verses.commentary:
37:16 This is a symbol of the reuniting of Israel's tribes that politically split in
922 B.C. under Solomon's son, Rehoboam (Judah, Benjamin, Simeon,
and most of Levi) and the Emphraimatic labor leader, Jeroboam I, who took the Northern Ten Tribes.

Note the IMPERATIVES in this paragraph.

- "take," Ezek. 37:16, Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 542, KB 534)

- "write," Ezek. 37:16, Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 507, KB 503)

- "take," Ezek. 37:16, Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB542, KB 534)

- "write, Ezek. 37:16, Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB507, KB 503)

- "join," Ezek. 37:17, Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 897, KB 1132)

- "say," Ezek. 37:19, Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 180, KB 210)

- "say," Ezek. 37:21 Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 180, KB 210)

▣

NASB, NKJV, TEV, NKB, Peshitta, JPSOA
"stick"

REB
"one leaf of a

wooden tablet"

LXX
"rid"

NET
"branch"

The root, עצ (BDB 781, KB 863) has a wide semantic field connected to wooden objects.

- a tree, trees (Ps. 1:3)

- Tree of Life (Gen. 2:9,16; Prov. 3:18; 13:12; 15:4)

- wooden idol (Deut. 4:28; 28:36,64; Jer. 10:8)

- building material (Gen. 6:14; Deut. 10:3)

- piece of wood

- firewood (Deut. 19:5; Isa. 30:33; Ezek. 24:5)

- stake on which bodies are impaled (Gen. 49:10; Deut. 21:22-23; Josh. 8:29; 10:26,27)

- vine (Ezek. 15:2,6)

- fertility gods (Deut. 12:2; Ezek. 6:13; 20:28; Jer. 2:20; 3:9,13)

- figurative (i.e. Jdgs. 9:8; Isa. 10)

This context speaks of a figurative usage connected to the reunification of Israel and Judah.

- symbol of national Israel (if a vine)

- symbol of faithfulness (Ps. 1:3)

- symbol of ruling staff of Davidic monarch (Isa. 11)

Special Topic: Trees

verses.zh: 你要使这两根木杖接连为一，在你手中成为一根。
verses.en: Join[NOTE:1] them as one stick;[NOTE:2] they will be as one in your hand.
notes: Heb “bring near.”
Heb “one to one for you for one stick.”
verses.commentary:
37:17-22 The one God will have one people, with one leader, in one place! This sense of "oneness" is
also found in Eph. 4:4-6. It only makes sense that the one God (i.e. monotheism) who made all humans in His
image (Gen. 1:26-27) for fellowship, and who promised to redeem all humans in Gen. 3:15, would provide a way
(i.e. Christ, cf. John 1:12; 3:16; 4:42) for all humans to come into this fellowship (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13;
1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14; see Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan).

In this context the oneness refers to a reunification of Israel and Judah. The people of God
will be united again.

This text is a foreshadowing of the NT oneness! Monotheism demands a universal fulfillment
to those who believe, not to those who can document their lineage.

My biases are showing in this chapter! I pray they are biblically based!

Special Topic: Monotheism

verses.zh: 你本国的子民问你说：『这是甚么意思？你不指示我们么？』
verses.en: When your people[NOTE:1] say to you, ‘Will you not tell us what these things mean?’
notes: Heb “the sons of your people.”
verses.commentary:
37:18 Ezekiel has been asked and has responded to several questions by the exiled Israelite community
(cf. Ezek. 12:9; 21:7; 24:19).

verses.zh: 你就对他们说：主耶和华如此说：『我要将约瑟和他同伴以色列支派的杖，就是那在以法莲手中的，与犹大的杖一同接连为一，在我手中成为一根。』
verses.en: tell them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look, I am about to take the branch of Joseph that is in the hand of Ephraim and the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will place them on the stick of Judah[NOTE:1] and make them into one stick—they will be one in my hand.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I will place them on it, that is, on the stick of Judah.”
The reunification of Israel and Judah is envisioned as well in Ezek 33:23, 29; Jer 3:18; 23:5-6; Hos 1:11; Amos 9:11.

verses.zh: 你所写的那两根杖要在他们眼前拿在手中，
verses.en: The sticks you write on will be in your hand in front of them.

verses.zh: 要对他们说，主耶和华如此说：我要将以色列人从他们所到的各国收取，又从四围聚集他们，引导他们归回本地。
verses.en: Then tell them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look, I am about to take the Israelites from among the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from round about and bring them to their land.

verses.zh: 我要使他们在那地，在以色列山上成为一国，有一王作他们众民的王。他们不再为二国，决不再分为二国；
verses.en: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over them all. They will never again be two nations and never again be divided into two kingdoms.[NOTE:1]
notes: Jeremiah also attested to the reuniting of the northern and southern kingdoms (Jer 3:12, 14; 31:2-6).

verses.zh: 也不再因偶像和可憎的物，并一切的罪过玷污自己。我却要救他们出离一切的住处，就是他们犯罪的地方；我要洁净他们，如此，他们要作我的子民，我要作他们的　神。
verses.en: They will not defile themselves with their idols, their detestable things, and all their rebellious deeds. I will save them from all their unfaithfulness[NOTE:1] by which they sinned. I will purify them; they will become my people, and I will become their God.
notes: Heb “their dwellings.” The text as it stands does not make sense. Based on the LXX, a slight emendation of two vowels, including a mater lectionis, yields the reading “from their turning,” a reference here to their turning from God and deviating from his commandments. See BDB 1000 s.v. מְשׁוּבָה, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:407.
verses.commentary:
37:23 It is true that the exile cured God's people of idolatry, but unfortunately other sins returned as
the book of Malachi and interbiblical history show.

YHWH does cleanse His people, but the pull of the fallen nature traps them again. They need
a new nature which only comes with the new covenant (Ezek. 36:22-36; Jer. 31:31-34; Joel 2:28-32).

There is a manuscript variant in this verse.

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"dwelling places"

NRSV
"all their apostasies into

which they have fallen"

TEV
"all the ways in which they

sin and betray Me"

NJB
"the acts of infidelity

which they have committed"

JPSOA
"in all their settlements"

LXX
"all their transgressions"

The MT has מושבתיהם, "their dwellings" (BDB 444),
but many modern translations have משובתיהם, "their backslidings"
(BDB 1000). This kind of reversal of letters is surely possible in hand-copied manuscripts over an extended period of time. The
UBS Text Project, p. 125, gives the LXX a "C" rating.

Special Topic: Textual Criticism

verses.zh: 「我的仆人大卫必作他们的王；众民必归一个牧人。他们必顺从我的典章，谨守遵行我的律例。
verses.en: “‘My servant David will be king over them; there will be one shepherd for all of them. They will follow[NOTE:1] my regulations and carefully observe my statutes.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “walk [in].”
Heb “and my statutes they will guard and they will do them.”
verses.commentary:
37:24 "My servant David will be king over them" This is a Messianic title and shows the new-covenant focus
of this context (cf. Ezek. 34:23-24; Isa. 55:3-5; Jer. 30:9; Hosea 3:5).

It is surely possible that a new Davidic ruler, with a heart towards YHWH, will be manifested
in order to fulfill 2 Sam. 7:16; Psalm 89; and Gen. 49:10! This ideal, godly king became a rallying hope for
a godly people and the fulfillment of the conditional covenant promises. David was sinful, yet forgiven,
so too, Israel! Restoration and salvation are the work of God (i.e. new heart and new spirit), but the new
covenant must be received and walked in!

Special Topic: My Servant

Special Topic: Messiah

Special Topic: Messianic Era

▣ "they will walk in My ordinances, and keep My statutes, and observe them" For the terms

The VERB "walk" (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT) denotes a lifestyle obedience,

God's covenant people will be an obedient, godly people. This does not denote sinlessness,
but a heart for God and His word (cf. 1 John 3:6,9). By their fruits you shall know them (Matt. 7:15-23,
i.e. false prophets).

37:25, 26 "forever. . .everlasting. . .forever" This word (BDB 761) must be dealt with in context

verses.commentary:
37:26 "a covenant of peace" This same period of restoration is discussed in chapts. 16 and 20 (also called "the
eternal covenant," cf. Isa. 24:5; 55:3; 61:8; Jer. 32:40; 50:5; Ezek. 16:60).

The full phrase "covenant of peace" is mentioned in Ezek. 34:25. The covenant of peace is contingent on
repentance, trust/faith/belief, obedience, and perseverance, as is the "new covenant" fully clarified in the NT. It is free from a
sovereign God, but it has requirements (cf. Eph. 2:8-10)! The very concept of "covenant" implies responsibilities on both parties!

▣ "an everlasting covenant" The NIV Study Bible, p. 1279, has a good footnote about this. The phrase
is used sixteen times in the OT. Here are some examples.

- Noah, Gen. 9:16

- Abraham, Gen. 17:7,13,19 (cf. Ps. 105:9-10)

- David, 2 Sam. 23:5 (cf. Ezek. 7:12; Isa. 55:3)

- the "new covenant," Jer. 32:40 (cf. Ezek. 31:31-34; 50:5)

- earlier in Ezekiel, 16:60

- new Israel, Isa. 61:8

It is found most often in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 24:5; 55:3; 61:8).

37:26-27 "My sanctuary. . .My dwelling place" This obviously refers to a rebuilt temple in Jerusalem. The
question is, "When do these verses become a reality?"

In context, this refers to the decree of Cyrus II in 538 B.C., which allowed all the
exiled people groups, including the inhabitants of Israel and Judah, to return home and rebuild their national temples
at the expense of the Persian government.

For Israel and mostly Judah, this is recorded in

- Ezra

- Nehemiah

- Malachi

- possibly Obadiah and Joel

verses.commentary:
37:28 God wants a righteous people who reflect His character to the nations. Israel was meant to be
"a kingdom of priests" (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), but this wonderful call turned into an elitism! The goal of
creation is not Israel, but the whole world in fellowship with its Creator. Monotheism cannot become
a weapon of exclusivism. It must become a promise of inclusion!

▣ "I am the Lord who sanctifies Israel" YHWH transfers His holiness to
His people (cf. Ezek. 20:12). They are holy because of their relationship to Him. Now this positional
sanctification must become fleshed out.

Special Topic: Sanctification

▣ "when My sanctuary is in their midst forever" YHWH's sanctuary was abandoned by Him in chapters 8-10.
Now Ezekiel asserts it will return to a sanctified, united Israel under a new Davidic ruler. Chapters 40-48
are a graphic symbol of this new day. This may be an allusion to Exod. 25:8.

However, as the temple was central in the OT, Jesus, the true temple, becomes central in the
NT (cf. Matt. 26:61; 27:40; Mark 14:58; 15:29; John 2:19; Acts 6:14). You may say to yourself, why bring
Jesus into Ezekiel? He is the fulfillment of the OT. It is no longer about Israel (cf. John 8:31-59).
These OT symbols and prophecies have their ultimate fulfillment and expansion through Him!

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This section of Ezekiel (i.e. Ezek. 33-39) is confusing to me because

- it is surprising that Edom is condemned again in Ezek. 35 after it was dealt with in Ezek. 25:12-14.

- it is surprising that after Israel's marvelous restoration she is attacked again by surrounding nations (i.e. Ezek. 38-39).

This section sets the theological stage for John's vision in Revelation 19-20. As surprising as it is, the truth is clear. Spiritual
restoration will be followed by conflict (cf. Dan. 9:24-27)! However, a time of temporary victory will be followed by a time of ultimate
victory over evil (i.e. the new covenant's consummation). It is surely possible that Edom, as well as Gog, Magog, Meshech, and Tubal,
are imagery for the pervasive evil which attacks God's people again and again.

- The final literary unit (Ezek. 40-48) is a way of showing that the spiritual apostasy of Ezek. 8-10 is over and YHWH's earthly throne is restored
to its special place (i.e. the Ark). The last vision is one of ultimate, complete victory (i.e. symbolized lby a new temple).

- However, if it is true that one must interpret the OT through the eyes of the NT, then the book of Hebrews tells believers that Ezekiel was a
partial, temporary divine revelation (cf. Heb. 1:1). Progressive revelation negates a new temple! Even 2 Thess. 2:4 must be seen as a Greek
temple (i.e. "take his seat," there is no seat in a Jewish temple). A current popular theology (i.e. dispensationalism) focuses on Israel and
Jerusalem, thereby reading the NT through the eyes of the OT. The NT must have priority! The focus of the gospel is Jesus and His death
for all humans, not Israel! Please look at (Special Topic: Why are OT Covenant Promises so Different
from NT Covenant Promises? and Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan).
Who are the "covenant people" now? This is the question!!

For a good video on this issue, see Steve Gregg's YouTube video, "Deconstructing Dispensationalism"

- רוח (BDB 924, KB 1194-1201, also used extensively in Ezek. 1,3,11,42; see
Special Topic: Breath, Wind, Spirit)

- breath, Ezek. 37:5,6,8,9 (twice),10

- wind, Ezek. 37:9

- חיה (BDB 310, KB 309, also used extensively in Ezekiel 18, 33)

- live, Ezek. 37:3,9,14

- come to life, Ezek. 37:5,6,10

- כתב, write (BDB 507), Ezek. 37:16 (twice), 20 (cf. Ezek. 2:10; 13:9; 24:2; 43:11)

- נבא, prophesy, Ezek. 37:4,7 (twice), 9 (twice), 10,12 (BDB 612, KB 659); see
Special Topic: Prophecy (OT)

- There may be a shift in imagery from a battlefield, full of the unburied, sun-bleached bones in Ezek. 37:1-11 (esp. Ezek. 37:10), to a
graveyard in Ezek. 37:12. We must remember this is highly symbolic Hebrew poetic prophecy. Ezekiel is a precursor to the interbiblical
apocalyptic literature. However, this chapter is not apocalyptic!

- Especially in a prophetic book like Ezekiel we must familiarize ourselves with the genre of prophecy. Three books
have helped me navigate these turbulent waters!

- How to Read the Bible For All Its Worth by Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart (pp. 181-204)

- Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic by D. Brent Sandy

- Cracking Old Testament Codes by D. Brent Sandy and Ronald Giese

- Also note Introduction to Biblical Interpretation by Klein, Blomberg, and Hubbard, pp. 292-312.

Many personal and denominational dragons (i.e. presuppositions and biases) live in these waters!

Special Topic: Prophecy (OT)

- After thinking through this whole issue of a restored geographical Israel, it becomes obvious why dispensationalism wants to separate
Israel and the church. This relatively new system of thought (see C. Bass, Backgrounds to Dispensationalism) takes seriously OT
Scripture (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). If OT prophecy is literally true (and I am not sure this is true in light of genre studies, cf. Plowshares and
Pruning Hooks; Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic by D. Brent Sandy. I think prophecies, for the most
part, are conditional), there must be an end-time national Israel and we learn from Ezek. 38-39 that it will be invaded during a golden age of peace and security.

The problem comes when this is not the theological agenda of the NT, which focuses on believers and
unbelievers and depreciates the Jew-Gentile divide (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13). At this point the theological options are difficult to make.

- OT Scripture has been fulfilled and superceded by the gospel (i.e. Matt. 5:17-19,21-48). This means that all the promises of YHWH
to Israel concerning her restoration to Canaan must be seen as

- fulfilled in Jesus (the Davidic Messiah)

- abbrogated because of Israel's continued covenant violations

- Israel was surely an initial part of YHWH's revelatory plan, but not the ultimate goal.

- Israel is no longer the key to world evangelization

- the OT prophesies about national Israel must be rethought (neither Jesus nor any NT writer reaffirms a
national promise to Israel)

- the whole theological system of dispensationalism which posits

- all prophecies must be literally fulfilled to national Israel (see Special Topic: Prophecy [OT])

- the church and Israel are totally separate

- there will be a secret rapture of the church so that OT prophecies can be literally fulfilled to Israel

- the millennium (and the book of Revelation) are primarily about Israel and not the church must be rejected as sincere and clever,
but misguided! Its presuppositional grid is more logical than biblical!
